clue.text: Competitive rider who's off at present for festive season?

indicators.note: off here means out of order, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

parts.note: a woolly jumper is the classic Christmas present

explanation.surface: A rider takes a break from competing over the Christmas holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' reshuffles WHOS into SHOW; 'at' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A show jumper rides a horse over fences in equestrian competitions.

clue.text: Nap that is taken on board with thanks

indicators.note: taken on means received aboard, so one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, the vessel you go on board
IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: A sailor takes a nap aboard ship and is thankful for it.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is everyday British slang for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A siesta is an afternoon sleep, a short rest of the kind taken in hot countries.

clue.text: Dark film has length cut after Oscar

indicators.note: after places the second piece behind the first

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: length cut means the L for length is removed

parts.note: plaque is the thin film that forms on teeth

explanation.surface: A dark film is shortened after winning an Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' looks cinematic but is the deposit on teeth; L is the usual abbreviation for length.
explanation.definitionFit: Something opaque lets no light through, so it is dark or murky.

clue.text: Game lure was set up on gravel

parts.note: a jig is a fishing lure jerked through the water

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the word is turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: to gravel is an old American sense of to puzzle or perplex

explanation.surface: A fishing lure has been laid out on a gravel bed.
explanation.walkthrough: GRAVEL as a verb means to baffle; 'on' is a link word joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A jigsaw puzzle is a picture cut into pieces to be fitted back together, a pastime or game.

clue.text: Spy and his boss, say, getting Spanish approval

parts.note: M is the head of the secret service who gives James Bond his orders
ole is the cry of approval at a bullfight

explanation.surface: A spy and his chief are cheered in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a spy who works inside an organisation, often for years, before being activated.

clue.text: Those assisting passage of sailors following course

indicators.note: following places the second piece after the first

parts.note: Epsom is the racecourse in Surrey where the Derby is run
old salts are experienced sailors

explanation.surface: Sailors help a ship make its passage along a set course.
explanation.walkthrough: EPSOM is a famous English racecourse. 'passage' is not a voyage but the bowels' movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom salts are a laxative, so they help things pass through the gut.

clue.text: Crack cut by drug dealer's equipment

indicators.note: cut means a word is docked of its final letter

parts.note: to have a crack at something is to have a shot at it
E is the usual abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Crack cocaine is being cut with another drug by a dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's drug dealer is a card dealer: a shoe is the box that holds the decks at a casino table. 'cut' docks the T from SHOT.
explanation.definitionFit: In casinos a shoe is the box from which a croupier deals playing cards.

clue.text: Printout from PC in bold

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside another

parts.note: hardy means bold or brave
a PC is a police constable, a cop

explanation.surface: A document printed off a computer appears in bold type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PC' suggests a computer, fitting 'Printout', but it is a police constable.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard copy is a paper version of a document, as opposed to one on screen.

clue.text: Prayers, for example, describing meat one put out

indicators.note: describing means drawing around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: EG is short for exempli gratia, for example

indicators.note: put out means the given letter is expelled

parts.note: venison is the meat of deer
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A grace before a meal describes the meat that has been served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' signals the container: the meat loses its I for one under 'put out' before EG wraps round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican evening service of prayers, also called vespers.

clue.text: Preacher sent via potentially captivating setter?

indicators.note: captivating means holding captive, so one piece is enclosed by the other
potentially says these letters could become something else when rearranged

parts.note: a gel is something that sets, like jelly or hair gel

explanation.surface: A crossword setter might be able to win people over with his clues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potentially' rearranges SENT VIA into EVANIST, and 'captivating' puts GEL inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An evangelist is someone who preaches the Christian gospel.

clue.text: Brought back beer for drinks on the house

indicators.note: back says the extracted letters are read in reverse order
Brought means fetched out, so the letters are drawn from inside the words beer for

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A barman brings back beer that is served without charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave the hidden step no signal word; 'Brought' does that job, with 'back' turning the letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: Drinks on the house are given at no charge by the bar, costing the customer nothing.

clue.text: City proud to work with ITV's output

indicators.note: to work means to be worked over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A proud city works alongside a TV channel on its programmes.
explanation.walkthrough: ITV is a British commercial television network.
explanation.definitionFit: Productivity is the rate of output of work or goods.

clue.text: Bird out at sea ahead of vessel

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of the word before it are jumbled

parts.note: a can is a container, a vessel for holding liquid

explanation.surface: A seabird flies out over the ocean in front of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The toucan is a tropical bird with a huge colourful beak.

clue.text: Welcomes European writing about support

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing
a brace is a support or prop

explanation.surface: A European writer welcomes someone and writes in support of them.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace someone is to hug them, and so to welcome them warmly.

clue.text: Resignation from catholic church in fit over topless ball?

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the first piece above the second
in puts one piece inside another

parts.note: apt means fit or suitable
CE stands for Church of England

indicators.note: topless means the word has lost its first letter

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Someone resigns from the Catholic Church after an outburst over a topless ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Resignation is passive acceptance of something you cannot change.

clue.text: Second best with likely winners back in trim

parts.note: the pick of the bunch is the best
and means together with

indicators.note: back says the word is read in reverse order

parts.note: a nap is a racing tipster's most confident tip, a horse thought likely to win

explanation.surface: A racing tipster picks out the likely winners in second place.
explanation.walkthrough: A NAP is British racing slang for a tipster's best bet of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Spick and span describes something neat and clean, which is what trim means as an adjective.

clue.text: Secret coteries disbanded

indicators.note: disbanded means broken up, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Secret cliques have been broken up.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is understood only by an inner circle, so it is private or hidden.

clue.text: Attack community undermining foreign aid

indicators.note: undermining in a down clue puts the second piece underneath the first
foreign suggests something strange, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a tribe is a community of people

explanation.surface: A community attacks foreign aid and undermines it.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal onslaught against someone.

clue.text: Disappointment with cement mixer

parts.note: a swizzle, or swizz, is British slang for a swindle or letdown
to cement is to make things stick together

explanation.surface: Someone is let down by the quality of a cement mixer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cement mixer' reads as one thing, but the definition is just 'mixer'. SWIZZ or SWIZZLE is British schoolchild slang for a disappointing swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: A swizzle stick is a small rod used to stir cocktails, a mixer for drinks.

clue.text: Little devil-like creature

parts.note: an imp is a little devil
a la is French for in the style of, like

explanation.surface: A small creature that looks rather like a devil.
explanation.definitionFit: The impala is an African antelope, an animal or creature.

clue.text: Test wood frames for climbing plant

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards
frames means surrounds, as a frame does a picture

parts.note: elm is a wood
a try is a test or attempt

explanation.surface: Wooden frames are tested for a climbing plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing plant' reads as one phrase but 'climbing' is the reversal signal; 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Myrtle is an evergreen shrub with fragrant white flowers.

clue.text: Full coverage of dazed boxing champion?

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: totty is an old Scots word for dizzy or muddled
Muhammad Ali was the famous heavyweight boxing champion

explanation.surface: A newspaper gives full coverage of a boxing champion left dazed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' looks like part of the sport but signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Totality is the phase of a total eclipse when the sun or moon is completely covered.

clue.text: Alarm seen in Tardis, maybe

indicators.note: seen in says the letters can be found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Alarm is spotted aboard Doctor Who's time machine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tardis is the time-travelling police box in the British TV series Doctor Who.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismay is a feeling of alarm or distress at something unexpected.

clue.text: Fan clubs of old league

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
o' is a shortened form of of, as in will-o'-the-wisp

explanation.surface: A supporter of football clubs from an old league.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan' looks like a supporter but is the verb, to blow air on.
explanation.definitionFit: To fan something is to blow air over it and lower its temperature.

clue.text: One offering pork pies around bar

indicators.note: around signals that the word is turned round

parts.note: pork pies is Cockney rhyming slang for lies, so the person telling them is a fibber

explanation.surface: Someone offers pork pies around a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: PORK PIES is Cockney rhyming slang for lies.
explanation.definitionFit: A rail is a bar, as in a towel rail or a handrail.

clue.text: Booze home worker hides for times in charge

indicators.note: hides means conceals within, so one stretch is placed inside another

parts.note: in means at home
the ant is the crossword's usual worker insect
to can mean for, as in a toast to someone
X is the multiplication sign for times

explanation.surface: A home worker keeps drink stashed away for times when in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hides' means the home and the worker split apart to conceal the other three pieces between them; X is the multiplication sign.
explanation.definitionFit: An intoxicant is anything that makes you drunk, and alcohol is the commonest one.

clue.text: Boasted about shipping company

definitions.meaning: an old past tense of crow, meaning bragged
the people who man a ship

explanation.surface: A shipping firm brags about its own success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shipping company' is not a firm but a ship's company; 'about' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Crew is an archaic past tense of crow, to boast, and also the sailors working a vessel.

clue.text: After which head of supermarket belatedly flogged

indicators.note: head of picks out the first letter of the word that follows
flogged means beaten about, so the letters of the word before it are scrambled

explanation.surface: Supermarket goods are sold off late in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flogged' also means sold, which fits the surface; here it shuffles BELATEDLY to follow S.
explanation.definitionFit: Food past its sell-by date should no longer be on sale, so the phrase means the point after which it goes off the shelf.
